answer_1.quote: LLMs have demonstrated impressive capabilities across a wide range of natural language tasks, including question answering (QA), summarization, and reasoning.
answer_1.outputs: Answers and reasoning chains with attributed quotes

answer_2.quote: For datasets with text-based answers (i.e., 2Wiki, MuSiQue, and MoreHopQA), we use a mix of lexical and semantic measures... we report Exact Match (EM)... F1 score... Membership Match (MM)... Semantic Match (SM)... BLEU-4... ROUGE-L... BERTScore... METEOR... AlignScore.

answer_3.quote: We use GPT-4.1 to evaluate each step of the reasoning chain along four dimensions: (1) its relevance to the original question, (2) its usefulness in deriving the final answer, (3) the correctness of the subanswer, and (4) the completeness of reasoning... GPT-4.1 provides a binary judgment of whether the reasoning is sound and a 0-10 score assessing the overall logical flow across steps.
methods: LLM scoring of reasoning steps and overall chain

answer_4.quote: We conducted two preliminary clinical reader studies on MedQA... Each study involved asking clinically trained evaluators... to annotate 20 samples... For each reasoning step, clinicians were asked: (1) whether the subanswer was factually correct (yes|no), and (2) how relevant and useful the step was... They were further asked how logically consistent the entire reasoning chain was... In the second study... scored on a 0-10 scale for: completeness... correctness... and logical flow.
answer_4.guideline: Clinicians evaluated factual correctness per step (yes/no), relevance/usefulness per step (0-10), overall logical consistency (0-10) in first study; completeness, correctness, and logical flow (0-10) in second study
